holidays.name: National Lobster Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the spiny, claw-snapping crustacean beloved by butter enthusiasts everywhere. Seafood shacks and fancy restaurants alike celebrate with lobster rolls, bisque, and tails dunked in drawn butter.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday popular with the seafood industry and fans, especially in Maine and the Canadian Maritimes, where lobster fishing is a way of life.
holidays.funFact: Lobsters were once considered poverty food in colonial New England, served to prisoners and servants, and some servants reportedly had contracts limiting how often they could be fed lobster.

holidays.name: Smile Power Day
holidays.description: A day to flash your pearly whites and spread cheer, based on the idea that smiling is contagious and can improve your mood and the moods of everyone around you.
holidays.origin: Created as an unofficial observance promoting the power of a simple smile, inspired by the popular notion that smiling boosts happiness and goodwill.
holidays.funFact: Studies on the facial feedback hypothesis suggest that even a forced smile can slightly improve mood, though researchers still debate how strong the effect really is.

holidays.name: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day
holidays.description: A serious but important international observance that shines a light on the mistreatment of older adults and encourages communities to speak up, check in on seniors, and protect the vulnerable.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2006 by the International Network for the Prevention of Elder Abuse and recognized by the United Nations in 2011.
holidays.funFact: Purple is the signature color of the day, and people around the world wear it or light up buildings in purple to raise awareness.

holidays.name: Magna Carta Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the famous 1215 charter that told a king he was not above the law. Historians, lawyers, and history nerds raise a toast to the roots of modern rights and due process.
holidays.origin: King John of England sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede on June 15, 1215, under pressure from rebellious barons.
holidays.funFact: The Magna Carta was annulled by the Pope within weeks of being sealed, and it only became the legendary document we know after being reissued several times.

holidays.name: Nature Photography Day
holidays.description: A day for picking up a camera or phone and capturing the beauty of the natural world, from towering mountains to the suspiciously photogenic squirrel in your backyard.
holidays.origin: Established in 2006 by the North American Nature Photography Association to promote nature photography and conservation.
holidays.funFact: The very first photograph of a living subject in the wild is often credited to early wildlife photographers who needed days of waiting and cumbersome equipment just to snap a single shot.
